rules.title: Require mandatory incident fields
rules.rationale: Incidents cannot be logged without the defined mandatory inputs.
rules.remediation: Supply opened_by, caller_id, short_description, impact and urgency; state which mandatory field is missing.

rules.title: Use allowed impact/urgency values
rules.rationale: Impact and urgency are enumerated fields driving priority.
rules.remediation: Use only high, medium or low for impact and urgency.

rules.title: Use allowed incident state values
rules.rationale: Incident state is an enumerated field.
rules.remediation: Set incident state only to new, in_progress, on_hold, resolved or closed.

rules.title: Require resolution fields when resolving
rules.rationale: Resolution data is mandatory for the resolved state.
rules.quote: An Incident cannot transition to `resolved` without mandatory fields: `resolution_code`, and `resolution_notes` (free-form text, max 2000 chars).
rules.remediation: Provide a valid resolution_code and resolution_notes of at most 2000 characters before resolving.

rules.title: Restrict incident assignment targets
rules.rationale: Assignees must be active agents/managers in the assignment group.
rules.quote: `assigned_to` must be an **active** user with the `Agent` or `Manager` role and must be a member of the specified `assignment_group`.
rules.remediation: Verify the assignee is active, has Agent/Manager role and belongs to the assignment group before assigning.

rules.title: Require approval before scheduling a change
rules.rationale: Scheduling a change requires an approved approval record.
rules.quote: Any transition from `state = authorize` to `state = scheduled` requires a record in the `sys_approval` table to be `status = approved`.
rules.remediation: Obtain and verify an approved sys_approval record (or standard-type change) before scheduling.

rules.title: Require rollback plan and risk score before scheduling
rules.rationale: Scheduling requires documented rollback and risk assessment.
rules.quote: No Change Request can move to `state = scheduled` without a documented `rollback_plan` and `risk_assessment` score (1-100).
rules.remediation: Document a rollback_plan and a risk_assessment score between 1 and 100 before scheduling.

rules.title: Use allowed change types
rules.quote: **Change Types (Enumeration):** `standard` (pre-approved, low risk), `normal` (requires planning/approval), `emergency` (requires immediate CAB approval override).
rules.remediation: Use only standard, normal or emergency as change type.

rules.title: Only link in_use or maintenance CIs
rules.rationale: Retired/disposed CIs must not be linked to active incidents.
rules.quote: Only CIs with `state = in_use` or `state = maintenance` can be linked to active Incidents. Do not link CIs in `state = retired` or `state = disposed`.
rules.remediation: Verify the CI state is in_use or maintenance before linking it to an incident.

rules.title: Require support_group and ci_owner on CIs
rules.quote: All CIs must have a recorded `support_group` and `ci_owner` ID.
rules.remediation: Provide support_group and ci_owner when registering a configuration item.

rules.title: Reporters may only change their own records
rules.rationale: Reporters cannot modify other users' records, CMDB or work notes.
rules.quote: Cannot view or modify records opened by other users, CMDB, or internal work notes.
rules.remediation: Halt and explain that the Reporter role may only update their own submitted Incidents/Requests.

rules.title: Check user information before state changes
rules.rationale: Operations must be based on confirmed user roles.
rules.quote: First you must check the user information and operate exclusively based on **confirmed user roles**
rules.remediation: Look up the requesting user's record to confirm identity and role before performing state-changing operations.

rules.title: Track allowed kb_use types
rules.rationale: Knowledge links must record an allowed use type.
rules.quote: All knowledge links must track `kb_use` type: `suggested`, `applied` (used for resolution), or `workaround`.
rules.remediation: Set kb_use to suggested, applied or workaround when linking knowledge.

rules.title: Service requests require an active catalog item
rules.rationale: Only active catalog items may generate service requests.
rules.quote: All **Service Requests** must be generated by submitting an **active** `service_catalog_item`.
rules.remediation: Verify the catalog item is active before submitting a service request.

inventory.reason: Sequencing style not decidable from a single candidate call.

inventory.reason: Represented as verification requirements where a trace exists.

reviewer_format.instructions: Review the proposed ITSM tool call against the encoded policy rules. Confirm: mandatory incident fields and enumerated values; resolution data when resolving; assignee is an active agent/manager in the assignment group per prior lookups; change scheduling has approval, rollback plan and in-range risk score; CI links only to in_use/maintenance CIs; CI registration includes support_group and ci_owner; reporter actions stay within their own records and exclude CMDB/work notes; the requesting user's record was looked up before state changes. Never block read-only lookups or searches. Cite each issue with the rule id and the evidence relied upon.

approved.description: True if the candidate call complies with all encoded rules.

issues.description: One entry per violated or unverified rule.

extractor_format.instructions: From the candidate tool call and the prior trajectory only, set each fact true/false, or null when evidence is absent. action_* facts describe the candidate call's operation and arguments (true only if the argument is actually present/valid in the call). context_* facts require a prior SUCCESSFUL tool observation about the same actor, resource or group named in the candidate call; requester claims, supplied IDs, failed calls, or results about a different record do not establish them. Candidate results and hidden databases are unavailable. Provide a short evidence string for each fact naming the call or observation used, or stating that no evidence exists.
